pr_body:
Prior to this commit, while DataTierAllocationDecider accounted for
Desired Nodes (if available), it did not account for Node Shutdown
information.

As of this commit, nodes that are marked as shutting down for
removal from the cluster are ignored for the purposes of computing
the available data tiers. Desired Nodes configuration, if present,
takes precedence over node shutdown, as desired nodes should be
preferred if possible.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/97207
pr_comment: Hi @gwbrown, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Upon looking at this further, I've removed the `7.17.13` label as the code has diverged significantly enough that a "backport" would really just be an entirely new PR.

Thanks for the feedback; I'm out of the habit of coding on the hot path like this. I especially appreciate the recommendations for what to do instead - I've removed the `DataNodes` construction in favor of a cached map of roles to nodes in `DiscoveryNodes` and made sure to keep in mind the things mentioned, especially avoiding allocations and avoiding work that isn't strictly necessary.

review_comment: can we add a test that goes through the branch where we check that there're still more available nodes in the tier than the number of nodes leaving the cluster?

I am surprised `DataTierAllocationDecider#allocationAllowed(java.lang.String, org.elasticsearch.cluster.node.DiscoveryNode)` is not checking for the node shutdowns, is it already covered by some other decider (NodeShutdownAllocationDecider may be)?
It should be covered by `NodeShutdownAllocationDecider` as you pointed out.

Agreed, that case is covered by `NodeShutdownAllocationDecider`. We tried to keep the logic as isolated as possible, but in this case this decider needs to know about node shutdown so that it won't refuse to allocate shards with a tier preference to nodes without that tier when all the nodes in that tier are shutting down.
